We can use mocking for ValidationContext, JsonValidator, etc. Use Mockito.

Goal: comprehensive unit tests focusing on logic paths.

We'll create a test class with @RunWith(MockitoJUnitRunner.class). We'll mock ValidationContext, JsonMetaSchema, Config, etc.

We need to construct JsonSchema with a simple schema node (ObjectNode). Use Jackson's JsonNodeFactory.

Test combineCurrentUriWithIds: when id is null returns same URI; when id is fragment with no context returns null; when id valid resolves using URIFactory. We'll mock validationContext.resolveSchemaId to return id; validationContext.getURIFactory().create returns a URI.

Simplify: create schemaNode with fields: "id":"http://example.com/schema". Use simple node.

But getRefSchemaNode uses findAncestor().getSchemaNode() (which is root). If ref "#/foo", it will decode and node.at("/foo") . We'll set root node with child.

We'll mock metaSchema.getNodeByFragmentRef to return node for "#/defs". Provide simple.

Test findAncestor: simple.

Test initializeValidators: need validators map with mock validator that records preloadJsonSchema called. To have validators, we need read to produce validators. That method creates validators via validationContext.newValidator. We'll mock newValidator to return a mock JsonValidator. Provide schemaNode with property "type". Then call initializeValidators and verify preload called.

Test isDynamicAnchor: need schemaNode with "$recursiveAnchor": true. After constructing JsonSchema, dynamicAnchor should be true.

Test hasRequiredValidator/getRequiredValidator and typeValidator: schemaNode with required and type.

Test createExecutionContext: ensure returns ExecutionContext with CollectorContext.

We also test toString.

Because many methods are private, we test via public methods that trigger them.
